what: ORI-W: orientation reward std 0.8 AND weight 5.0, on the five orientation-limited clips
the_target: e09 e10 e13 e20 e21 -- the five unadopted clips the AUC decomposition calls orientation-limited, with an oracle bound of +0.318 of AUC each (0.377 -> 0.695) at a mean position error already down to 3.2 cm. About +0.053 on the entry mean if fully realised, which would pass crisiumnih at 0.58226.
why_the_previous_attempt_fell_short: Second-wave B4x raised the shaping std from 0.3 to 0.8 and gained +0.0206 on e00, 6% of the bound. At std 0.3 a clip 49.8 deg out earns exp(-(0.87/0.3)^2) = 0.0002 of the term, so there is no gradient; std 0.8 gives 0.31 and fixes that. But the weight stayed hardcoded at 1.0 against body_joint_position's 5.0, so the policy had a gradient and a fifth of a reason to follow it.
what_changed_to_make_this_runnable: patch_object_orientation.py gained --weight, reaching the YAML as well as the dataclass default (the YAML is what the runtime reads), with two tests; and brev/arm_flags.sh now passes V2D_OBJECT_ORIENTATION_WEIGHT through, as it already did for object_position's weight.
the_arm: Warm start each clip from its OWN actor -- the clean-reference fine-tune where one exists (e09, e10, e20, e21 from t1f_2c/t1f_3c), the shipped actor for e13 which was never fine-tuned -- with orientation std 0.8 and weight 5.0, start_curriculum, object_position std 0.08, seed 42, 50M steps. Own actor rather than the donor on purpose: this arm changes the REWARD, so the right starting point is a policy that already tracks position, and the donor transfer is a different axis.
the_bar: The standing Tier 1 rule: AUC improves and no other board regresses. The arm works if at least one clip adopts. Note the rule is demanding here -- these clips have tight shipped MPPE (e13 4.98, e20 2.08, e10 2.97, e21 4.79, e09 4.89), so an orientation gain that costs position will be refused, exactly as it refused e13 and e14 in the transfer arm.
that_tension_is_the_experiment: The decomposition says these clips have 0.318 of AUC sitting in orientation at 3.2 cm of position error. If the reward can collect some of it WITHOUT spending position, the rule adopts and Tier 1 AUC moves several places. If orientation can only be bought with position, every clip is refused and the headroom is unreachable under any rule that protects MPPE -- which would itself be worth knowing.
cost: 5 clips x 0.5 h x $0.68 = $1.70 plus bring-up, about $1.95
credit_note: The ledger says about $1.24 remains, but it said $0.40 immediately before a $1.56 box ran, so it is pessimistic. If the create fails for credit, that is the answer.
